claims.behaviour: The web-resource keeps its key, type and dependencies, but nothing ever loads it (see `end-of-life-decorator`, C-4144), because the licence state is fixed as licensed, valid and not expiring. No licence or maintenance hint appears on any page, for any user, and the page makes no REST call on its behalf. If an implementer ships a file in it, the file does nothing: nothing warns, nothing blocks.

The web-resource keeps its key, type and dependencies, but nothing ever loads it (see `plugin-manager-helper`, C-4151). Jira's plugin manager page shows nothing added by the plugin: no licence note, no warning and no extra button. If an implementer ships a file in it, the file does nothing: nothing warns, nothing blocks.

The screen of `/secure/admin/StructureLicenseDetails.jspa` (C-5212) shows the fixed state only: licensed, valid, not expiring, for the plugin and every recognised extension (SPEC.md section 1.1). It has no control to enter, change or remove a licence, and never shows a warning, an expiry notice or a blocked state. The page has no other view: the original's debug view is not part of the rebuild's behaviour.

No administration screen ever shows a licence warning, and no control on them is ever disabled on licence grounds. This holds for: configuration, defaults, backup, restore, migrate, maintenance, help tool, dark features and the setup guide. In particular 'Configure Scheduled Maintenance', 'Run Maintenance Now', 'Restore', the restore and migrate file name fields, 'Select Structures to Restore', 'Create Help tool' / 'Edit Help tool' and 'Clear' are always enabled, and the maintenance page's scheduled state depends only on whether scheduling is on.

When the web-resource is on a page (see `stats-offer-decorator`, C-4146 to C-4148), an information banner is put at the very top of the page header, once the document is ready. It reads 'Would you like to help us make <product> better by enabling anonymous usage statistics?' followed by three links: 'Yes, enable!', 'More details' and 'No, don't ask me again'. 'More details' opens the plugin's documentation in a new window, with the tooltip 'Open documentation in new window'.

Clicking 'Yes, enable!' does not follow the link. The offer banner slides up over 200 ms, then a success banner slides down over 200 ms. At the same moment `PUT /rest/structure/1.0/statistics/enableSending` is sent with no body. The answer is ignored: an error shows nothing and the success banner still appears. It records the setting locally; nothing is uploaded, now or later (C-4513).

Clicking 'No, don't ask me again' does not follow the link. The banner slides up over 200 ms and `PUT /rest/structure/1.0/statistics/dismissOffer` is sent with no body. The answer is ignored. The offer is gone for that administrator from then on (C-4514); no thank-you banner is shown.

The success banner reads 'Thank you! You can turn anonymous usage statistics on or off on the Support page.', where 'Support page' links to `<base URL>/secure/admin/StructureSupport.jspa` in a new window, with the tooltip 'Open Support page in new window'. It ends with a 'Dismiss' link, which slides the banner up over 200 ms. That click sends nothing to the server.

The setup guide page has the title '<product> Setup Guide', a one-sentence welcome note, and then these sections in order: required configuration, 'Optional Configuration', 'Anonymous Usage Statistics' (system administrators only) and 'Next Steps'. Each step of the required section has a done or alert marker, a heading and a text.

The heading of the required section is 'Required Configuration — Completed' when any project is enabled, otherwise 'Required Configuration' (the licence step always counts as done, C-5086). Licence step: done marker, heading 'License is Installed', and a sentence linking to the 'License Details' page `StructureLicenseDetails.jspa`. Projects step when done: heading '<product> is Enabled for One Project' for 1, '<product> is Enabled for <n> Projects' for more, and a sentence linking to the 'Configuration' page `StructureAdmin!view.jspa`. Projects step when not done: alert marker, heading 'Select <product>-Enabled Projects', a link 'Enable <product> for at least one project' (the URL of C-5087), and a few sentences explaining that the choice limits queries and hides the interface from users without access to such a project, ending with a link to the plugin's documentation.

'Optional Configuration' is a bullet list: 'Specify users who can work with <product>' (a link, followed by a note that a user also needs access to a structure-enabled project); 'Limit who can create new structures' (a link, with a note that the creator also needs general access); 'Adjust <product> defaults' (a link, followed by what can be changed there); and, for a system administrator only, 'Review maintenance settings' (a link, followed by what it adjusts). The URLs are those of C-5088.

For a system administrator the section 'Anonymous Usage Statistics' shows one of two states, by the stored value. Enabled: done marker, heading 'Anonymous Usage Statistics Is Enabled', and a sentence that it can be turned on and off and viewed on the 'Support Page' (`StructureSupport.jspa`). Disabled: alert marker, heading 'Anonymous Usage Statistics Is Disabled', the same sentence, and a link 'Enable Anonymous Usage Statistics'. The wording must not say that data leaves the instance, because nothing is uploaded (C-5089).

Clicking 'Enable Anonymous Usage Statistics' switches the section to the enabled state at once, without waiting, does not follow the link, and sends `POST /rest/structure/1.0/statistics/enableSending` with no body, ignoring the answer. The resource accepts only PUT, so the setting is not stored and the section shows disabled again on the next visit (as the original does).

'Next Steps' is a bullet list holding one entry: a link to the plugin's documentation with a short note on what it covers. The original's two other entries, a Marketplace listing to watch and a vendor support contact, are not part of the rebuild.

The resource gives server-rendered plugin pages their shared look: the theme, page layout and select styling, plus its images, for both Jira's light and dark colour modes. It has no script. Pages that use it depend on its dependencies `fonts` and Jira's `jira.webresources:autocomplete`. One behaviour is visible: a link that opens a structure in a new window reveals a small new-window marker on hover, focus and press.

The resource gives the three Help tool screens their styling and has no script. It depends on `help-widget`, `page-rc` and `widget-i18n`. On the screen with no help yet, the placeholder picture follows Jira's dark colour mode.

The resource has no file of its own. It only pulls in what the page needs: Jira's expander and date-picker, `page-rc`, `jquery`, `jsutil` and `widget-i18n`. The attribute troubleshooting screen must work with exactly these dependencies, and uses neither the expander nor the date picker.

The resource has no file of its own. It only pulls in what the page needs: Jira's expander and date-picker, `page-rc`, `jquery`, `jsutil` and `widget-i18n`. The performance audit log screen must work with exactly these dependencies.

The help tool box shows a question-mark marker with the title, then the content already rendered to HTML, then one entry per contact: linked to the user's profile, with avatar and display name. A narrow side bar next to the box repeats the title and has a chevron. When there are no contacts that part is empty.

In interactive mode only (the welcome page) the box can collapse into its side bar and expand again, with a 300 ms width animation. It toggles on a click on the side bar, on Enter while the side bar has keyboard focus (it can take focus), and on the `[` key pressed anywhere on the page. Collapsed, the side bar shows the question-mark marker; expanded, the chevron. The state is not remembered: a new page load starts expanded. Outside interactive mode (the admin screens) the box does not collapse, and clicks and keys on it do nothing.

`StructureHelp!view.jspa` (C-5074) has the heading 'Help tool' and the note 'Add a custom Help tool to the Welcome to <product> page.'. With no saved help: a button 'Create Help tool', a placeholder and the text 'This is only a preview'. With saved help: a button 'Edit Help tool', a 'Clear' control with a trash marker, a link 'View Welcome page' to `/secure/StructureWelcome.jspa`, and below them the help box in its non-interactive form. The Create or Edit button links to `/secure/StructureHelp!edit.jspa` and has keyboard focus when the page opens.

'Clear' does not post at once. It opens the shared confirmation dialog (`dialog-common`) with 'Are you sure you want to clear the Help tool? All content will be deleted.'. Confirming posts `StructureHelp!clear.jspa` with the page's `atl_token`; cancelling sends nothing.

`StructureHelp!edit.jspa` shows the heading 'Help tool', the same note, and a form: 'Title' (required, text field `title`), 'Content' (required, Jira's wiki editor, field `content`) and 'Contacts' (optional multi-user picker, field `contacts`, placeholder 'Enter username or email', filled from the contact details of C-5075). The contacts picker uses the plugin's multi-user picker and needs the resources of Jira's issue view context, which the page requests. The title field error is shown under the title and the content error under the editor.

The edit form has three submit buttons, each posting all fields to its own command: 'Preview' to `StructureHelp!savePreview.jspa`, 'Apply' to `StructureHelp!save.jspa`, and 'Cancel' to `StructureHelp!cancel.jspa`. All carry `atl_token`.

`StructureHelp!showPreview.jspa` has the heading 'Help tool' and the note, then the help box as it will look, non-interactive, and three buttons: 'Continue editing' (a link to `StructureHelp!edit.jspa`), 'Apply' and 'Cancel'. Apply and Cancel post to `StructureHelp!save.jspa` and `StructureHelp!cancel.jspa` with hidden fields `title`, `content`, `contacts` (the comma-separated keys) and `atl_token`.

The fragment of `/secure/StructureHelpDialog.jspa` (C-5084), with saved help, shows the title as a heading with a question-mark marker, the rendered content, and each contact with avatar and profile link; hovering a contact's name shows Jira's user hover card above the dialog. With no help it shows the heading 'No admin tips'. Both have a 'Close' link that closes the dialog.

Pages sit in Jira's administration frame in the section `structure-admin/structure-admin-main`, with this web item active. `wi-structure-admin`: configuration, projects and permission forms. `wi-structure-defaults`: defaults and its sub-pages. `wi-backup-link`, `wi-restore-link`, `wi-migrate-link`: their pages. `wi-maintenance-link`: both maintenance pages. `wi-support-link`: support, statistics, database troubleshooting, the synchronizer and performance audit logs, and attribute troubleshooting. `wi-attribute-sensitivity-link`: attribute sensitivity. `wi-help-link`: help tool. `wi-structure-setup-guide`: setup guide. The migration configuration pages use the section `structure-admin/structure-admin-other` with `wi-migrate-to-cloud-link`. The dark features page names the main section and no active item. The project settings page uses Jira's project administration frame with `wi-admin-project-structure`.

The page `StructureAdmin!view.jspa` (C-5098) has the title '<product> App Configuration'. First section 'Projects with <product>': '<product> enabled for projects:', then 'All projects', or 'None' when none is picked, or a boxed list of project names, then the button 'Enable/disable <product> in projects'. The section header has a help link to the plugin's documentation (tooltip 'Open related part of documentation in a separate browser window or tab'). Below it follow the nine permission sections, each with its title, its note if any, its label, and its value: the 'anyone' text, the 'nobody' text, or a boxed list of subjects, and an edit button.

to <product> | <product> users | Everyone | Nobody | Select <product> users. `createStructure`: Permission to Create Structures | New structures can be created by: | Select who can create new The note of the `synchronization` section (C-5099), which also appears on the support page, is a short paragraph: the synchronizers feature is being deprecated, none is in use and it is hidden from users, and installing new ones needs the dark feature `structure.feature.synchronizers.enabled` set to `true`.

`StructureAdmin!editAppPermission.jspa` shows a form with the permission's section title as both page title and heading, and its edit subtitle. Under the permission's edit label are two radio buttons named `permissionMode`: value `anyone` labelled with the permission's 'anyone' text, and value `selection` labelled 'Users in selected groups/roles', the second with the list of subjects beneath it. Then 'Add group/role' with its controls, and at the bottom 'Apply' and a 'Cancel' link to the cancel target of C-5104. On opening, the radio shows whether the permission is allowed for anyone.

Apply posts to `StructureAdmin!setAppPermission.jspa?permission=<key>` with `permissionMode`, `atl_token`, `returnUrl` when the page received one, and the hidden field `permissionSubjects`: the listed subjects joined by commas with no trailing comma, each being `group:<name>` or `role:<project id>:<role id>`. The list is sent in both modes. A second click on Apply while the page is submitting sends nothing more.

The subject list starts with the permission's current subjects in stored order. Each line reads 'Group: <name>', 'Project: <project> Role: <role>', or 'Project: Any Role: <role>' for project id 0, followed by a trash marker. An unknown project or role shows its raw id instead of a name. Clicking the trash removes that line and its entry from `permissionSubjects`. When the list is empty it shows 'No groups or roles selected'.

While the `anyone` radio is selected the subject list and the 'Add group/role' row are disabled: the add controls cannot be used, the Add button does nothing, and the trash markers do nothing. The subjects stay listed, and return to use when `selection` is chosen.

The 'Add group/role' row has a kind dropdown with 'Group' (`group`, the initial choice) and 'Project' (`role`), and an 'Add' button. For 'Group' one searchable picker of groups is shown; for 'Project' two searchable pickers are shown, project and role. Each picker starts on its first option; the project picker's first option is 'Any' (id 0). Changing the kind shows only its controls and updates the description line.

Clicking 'Add' appends the chosen subject to the list. When the subject is already listed, nothing is added and the existing line is highlighted briefly. Adding to an empty list first removes the 'No groups or roles selected' text. With no group available the group picker is empty, and 'Add' then adds a subject with an empty name (as the original does).

The three pickers search only in the browser, in lists the page received; no request is sent. With an empty search each lists the first N options in the order received, N being the limit of C-5105 (20 by default); for the project picker that is 'Any' and the first N-1 projects. With search text, options whose name matches are listed, shortest name first, at most N; 'Any' is not searched. When more match than are listed, a footer reads 'Showing <N> of <total> matching groups' (or 'projects', 'roles').

Below the row a line describes the subject currently chosen, updated when the kind or a picker changes. For `use`: ' will be enabled for all users in the '' group', '... in the project role '' for project '

'', or '... in the project role '' for any project that is enabled for'. For the others: 'Allow users in '' group to ', 'Allow users in the project role '' for project '

' to ', 'Allow users in the project role '' for any project that is enabled for to ', with X: create new structures, control synchronizers, access automation, configure generators, configure effectors, execute effectors, execute effectors on query results, manage global saved columns.

`StructureAdmin!editProjects.jspa` has the title 'Projects with <product>' and two radio buttons named `allSome`: `all` 'Enable <product> for all projects' and `some` 'Enable <product> for selected projects'. Under the second are two multi-select lists showing 25 rows, 'Selected projects:' (picked projects) and 'Available projects:' (the others), with the buttons '<< Enable' and '>> Disable' between them. The radio is set by the stored choice. While `all` is chosen both lists and both buttons are disabled.

'<< Enable' moves the options selected in 'Available projects:' to 'Selected projects:', and '>> Disable' does the reverse. Moved options are placed in the target list in alphabetical order for the browser's locale. Nothing is sent until Apply.

'Apply' posts to `StructureAdmin!setProjects.jspa` with `allSome`, `projectsList` (the ids of every option in 'Selected projects:', comma-joined, also in `all` mode), `atl_token` and `returnUrl` when the page received one. A second submit is ignored. 'Cancel' links to the page's cancel URL.

`StructureDefaults.jspa` has the title '<product> Defaults' and these sections in order: 'Default Structure' (with a help link to the plugin's documentation), 'Default View Settings', '<product> User Interface Defaults' and '<product> Automation Defaults', each with a short explanatory note, and, under the condition of C-5108, 'Other Defaults', with no note. The first has two halves side by side: 'System Default Structure' and 'Project Default Structures'.

The 'System Default Structure' part shows the label, then the structure's name as a link opening `/secure/StructureBoard.jspa?s=<id>` in a new window with its description as tooltip, or '?' when there is none. Its 'Change' button is a GET form to `StructureDefaults.jspa` with `selectDefaultStructure=true`.

'Project Default Structures' has a checkbox 'Show only projects with overridden default structure', checked on load, and a scrolling table: Project, Default Structure, and a 'Change' link. A project with no own default shows 'system default'. While the checkbox is checked those rows are hidden; unchecking shows them at once, with no request. When the checkbox is checked and every project uses the system default, including when there are no projects, a single row reads 'All projects are configured to use the system default structure'; otherwise that row is hidden.

'Default View Settings' shows 'Views Menu:' with one row per view (name in bold with its description as tooltip, the limit text when limited, and 'ID: <id>') and 'Default Views:' with one row per page that has a default view ('<page name>:' and the view's name). Its 'Change' button is a GET form to `StructureViews.jspa` with `id=0`.

'<product> User Interface Defaults' shows, each with a short help note beside it, 'Auto-switch (Issue Page):', 'Auto-switch (Project Page):', 'Keep Structure Selection When Navigating:' and 'Auto-minimize <product> Panel:', with the current values in the On and Off wording of the form. 'Change' is a GET form with `selectUIDefaults=true`. '<product> Automation Defaults' shows 'Default generation time limit (in seconds):' with its value and 'Change', a GET form with `selectAutomationDefaults=true`. 'Other Defaults' shows 'Allow manual adjustments of generated content:' with the On or Off wording and 'Change', a GET form with `selectOtherDefaults=true`.

The sub-page 'Select System Default Structure' has one dropdown 'System Default Structure:' named `sid`, listing the structures by abbreviated name with the description as tooltip, the current default selected, and a 'Change' button. It posts to `StructureDefaults!apply.jspa` with `selectDefaultStructure=true`, `execute=true` and `atl_token`. A `sid` error is shown under the dropdown.

The sub-page has the heading 'Select Default Structure for Project: <name>', the line 'Project: <name> (<key>)', and a dropdown 'Default structure for this project:' named `sid` whose first option is 'Use system default' (value -1), selected when the project has no default of its own, followed by the structures. 'Change' posts to `StructureDefaults!apply.jspa` with `selectProjectDefaultStructure=true`, `projectId`, `execute=true` and `atl_token`. A `sid` error is shown under the dropdown.

The sub-page '<product> User Interface Defaults' has dropdowns 'Auto-switch (Issue Page):' `autoSwitchIssuePage` and 'Auto-switch (Project Page):' `autoSwitchProjectPage`, whose options are the strategies of C-5112 with their stored codes as values, and two radio pairs with values `true` and `false`. `keepStructureWhenNavigating`: 'On - When going from structure widget to an issue page, show the same structure' and 'Off - On the issue page, the structure initially shown is chosen according to the Auto-Switch settings'. `autoCollapse`: 'On - <product> panel initially minimized if issue is not in structure' and 'Off - <product> panel is shown'. 'Change' posts with `selectUIDefaults=true`, `execute=true` and `atl_token`. Each field's error is shown under it.

The sub-page 'Select <product> Automation Defaults' has one required number field 'Default generation time limit (in seconds):' named `generationTimeDefaultLimit`, holding the current value, with the minimum and maximum of C-5113. The field accepts only digit keys, Backspace, Delete, navigation keys and Ctrl or Cmd with A, C, V or X, and normalises its value to a plain integer on each change (leading zeros go). 'Change' posts with `selectAutomationDefaults=true`, `execute=true` and `atl_token`.

The sub-page 'Other Defaults' has the radio pair `allowManualAdjustments`: `true` 'On - Manual adjustments of generated content will be enabled for newly created structure', `false` 'Off - Manual adjustments of generated content will be disabled for newly created structure', with the current value selected. 'Change' posts with `selectOtherDefaults=true`, `execute=true` and `atl_token`.

`StructureProjectSettings.jspa` (C-5116) sits in Jira's project administration frame, titled '<product> Defaults - <abbreviated project name>'. It lists 'Project:' with name and key. For an enabled project: '<product>: Enabled for this project'; 'System Default Structure' as a link opening in a new window, or '(structure not visible)'; and 'Project Default Structure' the same way, with a 'Change' button.

Clicking 'Change' on the project settings page, with no request, replaces the structure link with a dropdown `sid` (first option 'Use system default', value -1, selected when the project has no default of its own) and the button with 'Apply'. Apply posts to `StructureProjectSettings!apply.jspa` with `projectKey`, `sid`, `execute=true` and `atl_token`. When the page returns with a `sid` error it opens already in this state, with the error under the dropdown.

For a project not enabled, the page shows 'Disabled for this project' in bold and, for a user allowed to enable it, a link 'Select which projects are enabled for <product>' to `/secure/admin/StructureAdmin!view.jspa`; for others the text 'Please contact your Jira administrator to enable <product> for this project.'.

`StructureBackup.jspa` has the title '<product> Backup', a short note on what is and is not backed up (structure data as a zipped XML file, only relationships and references to items; Jira's own data is backed up with Jira's tool), and the warning 'Backup is only enabled into "export" directory in your Jira home.' when there is no export directory. Form: 'File name' with the directory path shown before the field `backupFilename`, and its error under it; 'Backup History' with checkboxes 'Include full change history in the backup. If off, only the current state of the structures is backed up.' and 'Include full change history of memos and planning tasks in the backup.'; and 'Backup Extensions', shown only when there are extensions, with one checkbox per extension. The button 'Create Backup' has access key S and posts to `StructureBackup!apply.jspa` with `execute=true` and `atl_token`. A second submit is ignored.

The overwrite page (C-5122) has the title '<product> Backup: Confirm File Overwrite', the warning 'File with that name already exists. Proceeding with backup will overwrite its contents.', the question 'Overwrite <path>?' with the path in bold, a button 'Overwrite File' and a 'Cancel' link. A second submit is ignored.

The result page has the title '<product> Backup Successful', the line '<product> is successfully backed up to:', and a read-only field with the destination path, which has focus with all its text selected when the page opens.

`StructureRestore.jspa` has the title 'Restore Structure from Backup', two notes that say the restore replaces all current <product> data and when to use it rather than Migrate (with a link to `StructureMigrate.jspa`), the warning 'During the restore operation, Structure will not be available.', and, when structures already exist, a warning that all current data will be removed before the import, with a link to `../ManageStructure.jspa?view=recent` in a new window. Form: 'File name (.xml or .zip)' with the directory path shown before the field `restoreFilename`, its error under it; 'Options' with the checkbox `restoreHistories` 'Restore structure history', checked on display. The button 'Restore' has access key S, submit name `restore`, and posts to `StructureRestore!apply.jspa` with `execute=true` and `atl_token`. A second submit is ignored.

The confirmation page (C-5133) has the title 'Confirm Clearing <product> Data', a warning that the current structure information will be removed and other Jira data is not affected, a note 'You can create a backup of the current <product> data first.' whose middle part links to `StructureBackup.jspa` in a new window (tooltip 'Backup Structure in a Separate Window'), the button 'Clear Current <product> Data and Restore It from Backup' and a 'Cancel' link to `StructureRestore.jspa`. A second submit is ignored.

The restore result page shows a success message '<product> data has been successfully restored from backup.', or, when aborted, a warning 'Restore process was aborted. <product> data was not fully restored. It is recommended that you restore again.'. For an unowned structure 1, a warning says the backup contains that structure with no owner, that automation does not work without an owner, and links 'Edit Structure Settings' to `<base URL>/secure/EditStructure.jspa?id=1` in a new window. Warnings follow the order of C-5138. Sub-headings are 'Structure "<name>" (#<id>):', 'Could not include the following items in the structure (all other items are included):', 'Could not include the following items in the change history (as a result, the change history may have become partially incorrect):', 'Could not restore the following synchronizers in structure (all other synchronizers have been restored):', and synchronizer lines read 'Synchronizer #<id>' with ': <message>' when there is one.

`StructureMigrate.jspa` has the title '<product> Migration / Partial Import', two notes that say structures are restored from a backup without affecting existing ones unless overwriting is chosen, that issues must already be in Jira and are matched by Issue Key, and when to use it rather than Restore (with a link to `StructureRestore.jspa`), and the warning 'During the restore operation, Structure will not be available.'. Form: 'File name (.xml or .zip)' with the directory path before the field `restoreFilename`, its error under it. The button 'Select Structures to Restore' has access key S and posts to `StructureMigrate!apply.jspa` with `execute=true` and `atl_token`. A second submit is ignored.

The options page has the title 'Select Structures to Restore', a note on choosing structures and overwriting, and a table with columns Action, ID, Name, Items, Projects, 'Has Synchronizers?', 'Has Adjustments?' (only when manual adjustments are enabled), 'Has History?' and 'Has Memo and Planning task history?', the 'Has...' columns reading Yes or No. Each Action cell has a checkbox `migrate-st-<id>` 'Restore', checked; when the structure would overwrite, also a checkbox `st-<id>-overwrite` 'Overwrite existing', unchecked. The Name cell shows the abbreviated name, an 'Archived' marker when archived, the description, and the warnings of C-5150 and C-5151. An unknown project shows its bare key as a warning.
Above the table are the buttons 'Clear Selection' and 'Select All', then 'Overwrite All' only when some structure can overwrite, and 'Deselect All Archived' only when some structure is archived.

Unchecking a structure's 'Restore' disables its 'Overwrite existing' block, greyed out and with its inputs not sent; checking enables it again. The 'Restore Selected Structures' button is enabled only while at least one 'Restore' is checked.

None of the bulk buttons submits the form. 'Select All' checks every 'Restore' and enables every overwrite block, leaving 'Overwrite existing' as it was. 'Clear Selection' unchecks every 'Restore' and every 'Overwrite existing' and disables the blocks. 'Overwrite All' checks every 'Overwrite existing', also in disabled blocks. After 'Select All', 'Clear Selection' and 'Deselect All Archived' the submit button's state is updated.
'Deselect All Archived' unchecks 'Restore' and 'Overwrite existing' of each archived structure, but leaves that structure's overwrite block enabled (as the original does).

The option 'Restore view settings for structures' (`migrateViewAssociations`), indented under 'Restore views', and its label are enabled only while 'Restore views' (`migrateViews`) is checked; disabled, it is not sent.

Under 'Options' the checkboxes of C-5152 read, in order: 'Restore structure permissions', 'Restore synchronizers', 'Restore manual adjustments', 'Restore structure history', 'Restore user favorites', 'Restore views', 'Restore view settings for structures', 'Restore structure properties', 'Restore structure item properties', 'Restore configuration', 'Restore dark features', 'Restore saved columns', 'Restore generic item history', 'Restore notes', then 'Restore <name> app data' per extension. There is no perspectives option. The warnings of C-5151 appear directly below 'Restore synchronizers' and 'Restore configuration'.

The form ends with 'Restore Selected Structures', which ignores a second submit, and a 'Cancel' link to `StructureMigrate.jspa`. When some structures are unrestorable a warning at the top links to the fragment `#unrestorable`, and after the form the heading 'Unrestorable Structures' introduces a read-only table with the same columns minus Action. With no selectable structure there is no form, only an error note saying that Jira must contain the projects referred to and suggesting Project Import, plus that table if any.

The migrate result page has the title '<product> Migration Completed Successfully' and the success message 'Selected structures were restored from the backup.'. Warnings use the sub-headings of the restore result page, and then 'Some structure perspectives were saved under new IDs:' with rows 'Perspective <old> has now ID of <new>.'. The warnings block also appears when only perspective ids changed.

`StructureMaintenance.jspa` has the title '<product> Maintenance' with a help link to the plugin's documentation, and a two-paragraph note on what maintenance does. Section 'Scheduled Maintenance': an info note 'Scheduled maintenance is enabled and runs daily.' with 'Last run:' and 'Next run:' times, or a warning 'Automatic maintenance is not scheduled. It is recommended to enable daily maintenance procedure.', then the button 'Configure Scheduled Maintenance', a GET to `StructureMaintenance.jspa` with `editScheduledParams=true`. An error note 'Last run of the scheduled maintenance finished with errors, please check Jira logs for details.' appears above when the last run failed.

Section 'Run Maintenance Now': while a process runs, the note 'Maintenance is running now.' with the link 'Open Progress Page', and no form. Otherwise 'Last manual run: <time>', the task list, and the button 'Run Maintenance Now', which posts to `StructureMaintenance!apply.jspa` with `execute=true` and `atl_token`.

The scheduled form has the title 'Scheduled Maintenance Settings' and the checkbox `scheduled` 'Enable scheduled maintenance'. Under it are two radio buttons named `crontabEnabled`: `false` 'Run daily at' with dropdowns `scheduledHour` (00 to 23) and `scheduledMinute` (00 to 55 in steps of 5) followed by the time zone in brackets, and `true` 'Crontab schedule' with the field `crontabSchedule` and a help link to the plugin's documentation. Then the task list. 'Apply' posts to `StructureMaintenance!apply.jspa` with `editScheduledParams=true`, `execute=true` and `atl_token`; 'Cancel' links to `StructureMaintenance.jspa`. After a crontab error the crontab radio is selected, the rejected text stays in the field, and 'Invalid crontab schedule: <text>' is shown. A form error is shown as an error note at the top.

Each task has a checkbox named by its key, a label and sometimes a description. In order: `backup` 'Backup <product> data', with sub-option `backup-saveHistory` 'Include full change history of all structures in the backup'; `removeOldBackups` 'Delete old backups'; `cleanupFavorites` 'Optimize favorites' (delete marks of users no longer in Jira, fix popularity counters); `cleanupForests` 'Optimize structures' (remove references to permanently unavailable items); `cleanupViews` 'Optimize view settings' (remove references to deleted views); `cleanupSynchronizers` 'Optimize synchronizers' (remove those of deleted structures); `cleanupStructureProperties` 'Optimize properties' (remove those of deleted structures); `removeOldSyncAuditLogRecords` 'Delete old synchronizer audit log records'; `reindexHistory` 'Reindex change history' (so entries appear in filtered activity streams); `cleanupPerspectives` 'Optimize structure perspectives'; `reindexStructures` 'Reindex structures' (recalculate which structures contain an issue); `removeOldChangeHistory` 'Delete old change history'; `removeOldEffectorProcesses` 'Delete old effector processes'; `removeOldProcessStates` 'Optimize old background processes' ('Delete old background process records'); and, on Data Center only, `cleanupItemTracker` 'Clear item events table' ('Highly recommended after removing or renaming Jira DC cluster nodes'). Values come from `maintenance-manager`'s form values: run-once values on the main page, scheduled values on the scheduled form.

Number fields, each a text field of at most 3 characters between a prefix and a suffix, with name | text | whether 0 is allowed. `removeOldBackups-minFilesToKeep` | 'Always keep <n> latest backups.' | no. `removeOldBackups-minDaysToKeep` | 'Always keep backups made during last <n> days.' | no. `removeOldSyncAuditLogRecords-daysToKeep` | 'Keep records for the last <n> days (0 means remove all).' | yes. `cleanupPerspectives-daysToKeep` | 'Delete perspectives that were not used during the last <n> days.' | no. `removeOldChangeHistory-daysToKeep` | 'Always keep changes made during last <n> days.' | yes. `removeOldChangeHistory-changesPerStructureToKeep` | 'Always keep <n> latest changes for each structure.' | yes. `removeOldEffectorProcesses-daysToKeep` | 'Always keep processes finished during last <n> days.' | yes. `removeOldEffectorProcesses-waitingPreviewHoursToKeep` | 'Always keep processes waiting for a preview confirmation <n> hours.' | yes. Each belongs under the task of the same prefix.

On submit each enabled number field is checked in the browser: a field that does not allow 0 needs an integer above 0, the others an integer of 0 or more. A failing field shows its message below it: 'Please enter a positive number.' for all of them, also where 0 is allowed; messages of passing fields hide. On the run-now form, and on the scheduled form while `scheduled` is checked, at least one top-level task must be checked (a sub-option such as `backup-saveHistory` does not count), otherwise 'Please select at least one task to execute.' is shown. Any failure stops the submit. A field that allows 0 shows that same message, although 0 is valid there (as the original does).

A task's sub-options and number fields are enabled only while the task's checkbox is checked and, on the scheduled form, `scheduled` is checked too. Disabled fields are skipped by validation and not sent.

On the scheduled form, unchecking `scheduled` disables all task checkboxes, both radios, the hour and minute dropdowns and the crontab field. With `scheduled` checked, the crontab field is enabled only for `crontabEnabled=true`, and the hour and minute dropdowns only for the other choice. Changes apply at once, without a request.

`StructureSupport.jspa` has the title '<product> Support' and these sections in order, each with a short note: 'Troubleshooting', 'Collecting Support ZIP', 'Synchronizer Audit Log', 'Performance Audit Log', 'Attribute Troubleshooting', 'S-JQL Troubleshooting', 'Database Troubleshooting', 'Anonymous Usage Statistics' and 'Clear Caches'. Link texts are 'View Synchronizer Audit Log', 'Download Performance Audit Log', 'View Performance Audit Log', 'Attribute Troubleshooting' and 'Database Troubleshooting'; the URLs are those of C-5192. 'Clear Caches' has the note 'Clearing caches might be needed if a cached value is incorrect' above the form of `ClearStructureCaches`.

On the support page the original's vendor links and vendor-addressed wording are dropped. 'Troubleshooting' holds a link to the plugin's documentation and no support request or e-mail link. 'Collecting Support ZIP' keeps its four numbered steps for collecting a ZIP with Jira's own tools (raise logging on Jira's Logging and Profiling page `<base URL>/secure/admin/ViewLogging.jspa` for package `com.almworks.jira.structure`; reproduce the problem; create the ZIP in the support tools at `<base URL>/plugins/servlet/troubleshooting/view/#support-zip`; pass it on), without saying where to send it. Notes do not name the vendor.

Section 'Anonymous Usage Statistics' has a note and a form with the checkbox `sendingEnabled` 'Send anonymous usage statistics', a button 'Apply' posting to `StructureSupport!apply.jspa` with `execute=true` and `atl_token`, and a link 'View Current Statistics' to `StructureSupport.jspa?showStatistics=true`. The original's note says data is sent to the developers and links to the vendor's documentation; here nothing is uploaded (C-5194), so the note must say the setting is only recorded locally.

The statistics page has the heading 'Anonymous Usage Statistics' and a help link to the plugin's documentation. It shows the report of C-5195 in a text area sized to the report, between 6 and 24 rows. Clicking the area selects all its text. A 'Back' link goes to `StructureSupport.jspa`.

`StructureAOSupport.jspa` has the title 'Database Troubleshooting', the section '<product> Tables Lock' with a note that tables are locked during a restore and may stay locked if it fails, and then the state. Locked: a short text that manual unlocking is possible if something went wrong, and the button 'Unlock Tables', posting to `StructureAOSupport!apply.jspa` with `execute=true` and `atl_token`. Unlocked: 'All good! <product> tables are currently unlocked.'.

`StructureAttributeTroubleshooting.jspa` has the title 'Attribute Troubleshooting', the warning 'Please note that the log may contain sensitive data. Please review it before sending.', a 20-row text area with the dump of C-5208, and the button 'Save to File', a GET to the same page with the submit name `save` and any non-empty value. It does not ask about leaving the page.

`PerformanceAuditLogView.jspa` has the title 'Performance Audit Log', the warning 'Please note that the log may contain sensitive data. Please review it before sending.', a 20-row text area with the dump of C-5202, and the button 'Save to File', a GET to the same page with the submit name `save` and any non-empty value (C-5204). It does not ask about leaving the page.

`StructuredJqlTroubleshooting.jspa` is framed as a general Jira page, not an admin page. It has the title 'Structured JQL Troubleshooting', a note with numbered steps: enter the structure's name or id and the query as in the `structure()` JQL function; tick the relations option only when asked to; click 'Run Query', and a correct query downloads the log file `S-JQL_Troubleshooting.zip`, and a form: 'Name' ('Name or ID of the structure to search in.'), 'S-JQL' (a multi-line field, described as the parameter of the `structure()` JQL function) and a checkbox 'Include output from relations (very verbose, please do not check unless we asked you to)', unchecked; then the button 'Run Query'. The form never submits as a page. The note's links go to the plugin's documentation and it does not name the vendor.

'Run Query' trims the query text and, when it is longer than one character and starts and ends with the same quote, `'` or `"`, removes that pair. Examples: `  'folder'  ` is sent as `folder`, `"a"` as `a`, `'a"` stays, a lone `'` stays. Only the outer pair goes. The structure text is sent as typed.
'Run Query' sends `GET /rest/structure/1.0/sjqlTroubleshooting/check?structure=<text>&query=<query>`, asking for JSON. The checkbox is not part of this call.

When the check succeeds the error box hides and the browser goes to `/rest/structure/1.0/sjqlTroubleshooting/logs?structure=<text>&query=<query>&includeRelOutput=<true|false>`, which downloads the ZIP (C-4502), so the page stays where it is. `messagePattern` is never sent.

On a 400 whose body is a non-empty JSON array, the error box shows the messages, HTML-escaped: the single message as plain text, or a bullet list when there are several. Any other failure, including a body that does not parse, shows the shared HTTP error report (a title and details, as `jsutil` formats it). The box stays visible until the next successful check, and no download starts.

`StructureDarkFeatures.jspa` has the title '<product> Dark Features and Fine Tuning' and the warning 'Please be careful! Entering an incorrect value for a property may lead to unpredictable results. Make sure you follow the instructions from support.'. On opening the page sends `GET /rest/structure/2.0/dark-features`. Until the answer nothing else shows. On failure it shows 'Failed to load property values. More information should be in the logs.' and no form. On success it shows the add form 'Property Key' (`darkFeatureKey`) with 'Add Property', and, when at least one row exists, a table with columns Key, Value and actions. Neither form triggers Jira's unsaved-changes warning.

Rows from the load keep the server's order. A key added later goes to the top of the table, and the table appears if it was hidden. Rows are never removed: a deleted key stays listed until the page is reloaded.
A row at rest shows the key, the value (empty when null) and two icons: pencil and trash. The trash icon is disabled, not clickable and out of the tab order, when the server's `removable` is false.

Clicking the pencil replaces the value with a text field holding the current value, focused, and the icons with a tick and a cross. The cross, or Escape in the field, leaves edit mode without a request and discards the typing. The next edit starts from the stored value again.

The tick, or Enter in the field, sends `PUT /rest/structure/2.0/dark-features` with the JSON body `{"key": <key>, "value": <text>}`, `Content-Type: application/json`. Success shows the new value and enables the trash icon. Edit mode ends on success and on failure. A failure shows no message and the old value stays.

The trash icon opens the shared confirmation dialog (`dialog-common`), medium size, with 'Property "<key>" will be removed and it will assume its default value. Proceed?'. Confirming sends `DELETE /rest/structure/2.0/dark-features` with the key as raw body text and `Content-Type: application/json`. On success the row stays, its value becomes the text of the answer (the JVM value, empty for a 204), and the trash icon is disabled. A failure shows nothing and changes nothing. Cancelling sends nothing.

Submitting the add form, by button or Enter, trims the text. A key already in the table shows 'This key is already in the table below. Click the pencil icon to edit the value.' under the field, clears the field and sends nothing; the row is not highlighted. Otherwise it sends `POST /rest/structure/2.0/dark-features` with the key as raw body text and `Content-Type: application/json`. Success adds a row from the answer, clears the field and any error. Failure shows the answer's text under the field and keeps the field. Typing in the field hides the error.

`StructureAttributeSensitivity.jspa` has the title 'Attribute Sensitivity Settings', a note of a few paragraphs on the trade-off between protecting data and all users seeing the same totals, and 'Loading...'. On opening it sends `GET /rest/structure/2.0/attribute-sensitivity` and also loads the attribute metadata needed for labels, through the shared attribute registry of `widget-bare`. When both finish the loading text goes and the form shows. When either fails, an error flag that cannot be closed says 'There was a problem loading data from the server. Please try reloading the page or contact your Jira administrator.' and the page stays on 'Loading...'.

The answer is cleaned in the browser. `sensitivityMode` outside 0 to 2 counts as 0. A spec lacking a string `id` or `format` is dropped. A non-object `params` is dropped. Each spec is normalised as attribute specs are in the widget. Specs are sorted by id, then format, then their JSON text. Saves send this cleaned list, so a dropped entry disappears from the server on the next save.

Section 'Attribute Sensitivity Mode' has a dropdown 'Mode' with Standard (0), Strict (1), Permissive (2), the button 'Change Attribute Sensitivity Mode', and a description: Standard: all attributes are sensitive except numeric and date-based. Strict: all attributes are sensitive. Permissive: no attribute is considered sensitive (recommended only if all your Jira users can see all issues). The button is enabled and emphasised only while the dropdown differs from the saved mode and no save is running, updating within 50 ms.

Every change is saved by `PUT /rest/structure/2.0/attribute-sensitivity` with JSON body `{"sensitivityMode": <n>, "nonSensitiveAttributeSpecs": [...]}`, always the whole settings. On success the page takes what it sent as the new state, without a reload, and shows a success flag that closes by itself: 'Attribute sensitivity mode has been changed.', 'Non-sensitive attribute has been added to the list.', 'Non-sensitive attribute specification has been edited.' or 'Non-sensitive attribute specification has been removed from the list.'. On failure a flag that the user closes says 'Error uploading changes. Please try reloading the page or contact your Jira administrator.', and the dropdown returns to the saved mode.

Section 'Additional Non-Sensitive Attributes', with the button 'Add Non-Sensitive Attribute', is shown unless the saved mode is Permissive; changing the dropdown alone does not hide it. Table columns: Name, Attribute Specification, and icons. Name is the attribute's suggested label, or 'Customized' when none can be made. Attribute Specification is the spec's JSON, also as tooltip. Icon tooltips: 'Edit non-sensitive attribute's specification' and 'Remove specification from the list of non-sensitive attributes'.

The Add dialog, titled 'Add Non-Sensitive Attribute' with buttons 'Add' and 'Cancel', and the Edit dialog, titled 'Edit Non-Sensitive Attribute Specification' with 'Update' and 'Cancel', are modal and have the same fields: 'Spec', a multi-line JSON text with the placeholder 'Enter attribute specification in JSON format. See documentation for details.' and no browser autocomplete or spellcheck; 'Attribute', the shared attribute editor; 'Format', a dropdown with the placeholder 'Select format...' and options Any format (`any`), Text (`text`), HTML (`html`), Number (`number`), Boolean (`boolean`), Time (`time`), Duration (`duration`). Add opens empty; Edit opens on the row's spec. Closing discards the fields.

The three fields stay in step. After typing pauses for 300 ms in 'Spec' (50 ms for the first update), when the text is valid JSON the attribute editor loads it and 'Format' shows its `format`; invalid JSON leaves the editor alone and clears 'Format'. A change in the attribute editor rewrites 'Spec' at once and updates 'Format'. Choosing a format sets `format` in the JSON of 'Spec' when that text parses; otherwise it has no effect on 'Spec'.
While a save runs, the fields in the open dialog are disabled, and any button inside its content area is disabled. The footer buttons stay enabled.

'Add', in this order: text that is not valid JSON shows an error flag 'Cannot parse JSON specification. Please check if it is valid.' that closes itself; a spec deep-equal to a listed one shows 'The specified attribute is already in the list.' the same way; otherwise `POST /rest/structure/2.0/attribute-sensitivity/validate` is sent with the spec as JSON body. A failed validation shows a flag the user closes, 'The entered attribute specification cannot be validated: <answer text>', and the dialog stays. A valid spec is appended and saved; on success the dialog closes, on failure it stays.

'Update', in this order: invalid JSON gives the same parse flag as Add. When the spec is unchanged, or the original is no longer listed, the dialog just closes and nothing is sent. A spec deep-equal to another listed one gives the duplicate flag. Otherwise it is validated as for Add, replaces the original in the list, and is saved. On success the dialog closes, on failure it stays.

The trash icon opens the dialog 'Remove Attribute from Non-Sensitive List', not modal, with the text 'If you remove an attribute from the non-sensitive list, its sensitivity will be determined by the selected Attribute Sensitivity Mode.', the question 'Would you like to remove the following attribute from the list?', the spec's JSON in a read-only box, and the buttons 'Remove' and 'Cancel'. 'Remove' saves the list without the spec and closes on success. When the spec is no longer listed it just closes.

When saving a removal fails, two identical error flags appear, 'Error uploading changes. Please try reloading the page or contact your Jira administrator.', and the dialog stays open (as the original does).

`SyncAuditLogView.jspa` has the title 'Synchronizer Audit Log' and the heading 'Find log entries' over a GET form to `SyncAuditLogView.jspa` that does not trigger Jira's unsaved-changes warning. 'Earliest entry': 'Date' `dateFrom` (Jira's date picker) and 'Time' `timeFrom`. 'Latest entry': 'Date' `dateTo` and 'Time' `timeTo`. 'Other conditions': 'Sync instance ID' `syncInstanceId` ('Display only entries for a synchronizer instance.'), 'Structure ID' `structureId` ('Display only actions for sync instances installed on a structure.') and the checkbox `showEmpty` 'Show entries without actions'. Date and time errors are shown under their fields. Buttons: 'Show' and 'Save to File' (submit name `save`). Fields hold the request's values.

Field help. `dateFrom`: 'Leave blank to show log entries from the beginning of time.'. `timeFrom`: 'Time of day (18:43), timestamp (1455715432286) or complete date and time (2016-02-26 19:11:09.460 +0400). Leave blank for midnight (if date is specified).'. `dateTo`: 'Leave blank to show log entries until now.'. `timeTo`: 'Time of day (18:44), timestamp (1455715433286) or complete date and time (2016-02-26 19:12:09.460 +0400). Leave blank for midnight.'. Tooltips: 'Date of the earliest log entry to display', 'Time of day of the earliest log entry to display', 'Date of the latest log entry to display', 'Time of day of the latest log entry to display', and, on `structureId`, 'Numeric structure ID. Leave blank to show entries for all synchronizer instances.'; on `syncInstanceId`, a tooltip says how to find the id on the synchronization settings page and that blank means all instances.
While 'Sync instance ID' holds non-blank text after trimming, 'Structure ID' is disabled, so it is not sent. This is applied on page load and on each change.

With no selected group, the page shows only 'No entries found.' below the form. Otherwise it shows the anchor `entries` and two tabs, 'View' (active) and 'Undo'. The View tab has the heading 'Selected log entries', the links 'Expand all actions' and 'Collapse all actions', the table, and then the cut-off warning of C-5286 or, when more than 5 groups are shown and none is cut off, '<n> entries displayed.'.

The third part of the cut-off warning is 'You may specify more precise time to select fewer entries.' when `timeFrom` or `timeTo` is empty; otherwise 'You may specify synchronizer instance ID to select fewer entries.' when no instance id is given; otherwise nothing.

Table columns: a checkbox column whose header checkbox selects all; 'Time'; 'Structure'; 'SIID' (tooltip 'Synchronizer instance ID'); 'Synchronizer'; 'Entry description', with the links 'Expand all' and 'Collapse all' in its header. A group's row holds the values of C-5287. A group with actions has a second row with its checkbox (only when undoable, C-5290, tooltip 'Select these actions for bulk undo') and 'Actions (<n>):', an 'expand' link that turns into 'collapse', and, when undoable, a link 'undo'. Actions are collapsed at first. The structure link opens in a new window.

Description and action data are JSON objects rendered as nested lists of `key: value` lines, in the object's order, on page load; a spinner shows in the cell before that. An object with `type` = `link` and non-empty `url` and `text` renders as a link. An object with more than 2 keys is collapsed behind a `+` control that turns into `-`; one with 1 or 2 keys is shown open. An empty array shows `[]`. An array of plain values is a bullet list of their text. A one-element array of objects shows that object inline. A longer one is a list of them. Each action at the top level of a group's list is shown open. Under the keys `jiraEvents` and `structureEvents`, and for objects of at most 2 keys, the object is shown on one line, not collapsed. Null shows as the text `null`.

'Expand all actions' and 'Collapse all actions' expand or collapse every group's action list. 'Expand all' and 'Collapse all' in the 'Entry description' header do the same to every collapsed object in descriptions and actions. No request is sent.

The header checkbox has the tooltip 'Select all actions for undo', changing to 'Deselect all actions' while checked, and is hidden when no group is undoable. It selects or clears all groups. It becomes checked when every group is selected and unchecked when none is. Selecting only some leaves it as it was.
Clicking a group's 'undo' link selects that group and switches to the 'Undo' tab. It keeps earlier selections and sends nothing.

With nothing selected, the 'Undo' tab shows the hint 'Select some actions in the View tab to undo them.'. Otherwise it shows the heading 'Selected actions', each selected group's actions with a checkbox that is checked (clearing it deselects the group here and in the View tab), and the button 'Undo'.

'Undo' disables the inputs of the Undo tab, shows a spinner, hides any earlier results, and sends `POST /rest/structure/2.0/synchronizers/undo` with `Content-Type: application/json; charset=UTF-8`, a 60-second timeout, and the body `{"actionGroups": [...], "syncModuleKeys": [...]}`: for each selected group in page order, its actions as the JSON text received with the page, and its synchronizer's module key at the same index.

When an answer carries `jobId`, the same POST is sent again at once with the body `{"jobId": <id>}`, with no delay and no limit on the number of calls, until an answer has no `jobId`. Each call has its own 60-second timeout.

When the undo ends, successfully or not, the inputs are enabled, the spinner goes, the 'Undo results' area shows with its old content cleared, and all selections are cleared. Success: a success message 'Undo has completed. See below the list of actions that we've taken.', then each non-empty group of `actionGroups` from the answer rendered as action lists; a group that is not valid JSON or is empty adds nothing. Failure: an error message 'Failed to retrieve undo results. The actions might or might not have been executed. For more information, please refer to Jira logs.', then 'Technical details', 'textStatus: <status>' and 'errorThrown: <error>'.
The 'Undo results' area has the heading 'Undo results' and the button 'Acknowledge', which hides the area. It is hidden until the first undo ends. The page's log table is not reloaded after an undo.

`StructureMigrationConfigurations!list.jspa` has the title '<product> Migration Configurations' and an information note: specify which structures go in each migration when using Jira's Cloud Migration Assistant, limiting each to structures whose projects are migrated or already were; with a link to the plugin's documentation. With no configurations: 'There are no configurations yet.' and the primary button 'Create new configuration'. Otherwise that button, then a table with columns Name, Structures, Created By, Status, Completed On and Actions. The button links to `StructureMigrationConfigurations!create.jspa`.

Each row's Actions cell is a menu button. Entries in order: for a draft 'Edit' (`!edit`) and 'Make Ready for Migration' (tooltip 'Change status to "Ready"'); for a ready configuration 'View' (`!view`) and 'Move to Draft' (tooltip 'Change status to "Draft" and edit this configuration'); for others 'View'; and always 'Delete'. The URLs are those of C-5180.

'Delete' in the list, and 'Delete Configuration' in the form, open the shared confirmation dialog (`dialog-common`) with 'Are you sure you want to delete this configuration?'. Confirming sends `POST StructureMigrationConfigurations!delete.jspa?id=<id>&atl_token=<token>` with `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, following redirects. When the answer was redirected the browser replaces the current page with the final URL, without any leave-page warning. A failed call, or one not redirected, shows nothing. Cancelling sends nothing.

The form page has the browser title 'Create Migration Configuration', 'Edit Migration Configuration' or 'View Migration Configuration' (C-5182, C-5183). It begins with a breadcrumb: a link 'Migration configurations' to `!list`, ' / ' and the name in bold; then a warning line 'Configuration name must match the migration name from the Jira Cloud Migration Assistant.'. Fields: 'Name' (required, `name`) with its error beneath; 'Status' showing the status marker and its description; one checkbox `migrate-ext-<key>` per extension labelled as C-5182; a warning note listing what does not carry over to the cloud (the projects of the selected structures must be migrated in the same or an earlier migration for their issues to appear, some automations including effectors are not supported, memos become folders, and only custom views associated with the selected structures are migrated), with a link to the plugin's documentation; and the heading 'Structures'. The `structureIds` error is shown under the structures.

Status texts, as label: description. Draft: 'The configuration is being created. When it's all set, click "Save and Make Ready for Migration."'. Ready: 'The configuration can be used to migrate to Cloud. To change it, move it to the Draft status first.'. Running: 'Migration is currently in progress.'. Done: 'Migration has been completed.'. Failed: 'Migration has been completed with errors.'.

For any status but Draft the form is read-only: the name, the extension checkboxes and the all-structures toggle are disabled, the structure picker and the Actions column are absent, and the Save buttons are absent.

Form buttons. Left: 'Delete Configuration' (tooltip 'Delete this migration configuration') when the configuration has an id; 'Move to Draft' when Ready, submitting to `!draft`. Right: for a draft, 'Save and Make Ready for Migration' (tooltip 'Save changes and change status to "Ready"'), submitting to `!publish`, and 'Save as Draft' (tooltip 'Save changes to this draft'), submitting to `!save`; and always 'Cancel', a link to `!list`. Submits carry `atl_token`, `id`, `name`, the extension checkboxes, `allStructures` when on, and `structureIds`.

'Cancel' with no changes just follows the link. With changes it opens the shared confirmation dialog with 'The changes made to this configuration were not saved. Are you sure you want to dismiss them?'; confirming goes to the list without a leave-page warning. A change is: the name differs from the page's initial value; an extension checkbox differs from its initial state; the all-structures toggle differs; or the id list differs, order included. Adding a structure and removing it again is no change.

Leaving the page by other means with unsaved changes triggers Jira's unsaved-changes warning. That covers the name, the extension checkboxes, the structure list and the all-structures toggle, although the last two are not plain form fields.

A toggle 'Migrate all structures and views', field `allStructures` with value `true`. On: the table is replaced by 'Structures: <total>' and `structureIds` is sent empty. Off: the table shows and `structureIds` is the listed ids joined by commas. The list is kept while the toggle is on, so turning it off brings it back.

The table has columns Name, Statistics, Description, and, when editable, Actions. With no ids a single row says 'No structures selected'. Rows follow the id list; a newly added structure goes to the top.

When editable, a search field with the placeholder 'Add structure' sits above the table. It sends `GET /rest/structure/2.0/structure?name=<text>&archived=true&limit=20&page=<n>&skip=<ids joined by dots>` after 500 ms of pause in typing, and offers `structures` with more pages while `haveMore` is true. An option shows the name, with the tooltip '<name> [#<id>]'. Picking adds the structure, unless it is listed, and clears the field. `skip` holds the ids listed at that moment, so listed structures are not offered.

Each row loads its structure with `GET /rest/structure/2.0/structure/<id>`, at most once per id per page. While loading, the row shows 'Loading...' across the first three columns; on failure 'Structure #<id> is unavailable' there. The Actions cell shows in all states. Loaded, Name is a link to `/secure/StructureBoard.jspa?s=<id>` in a new window, and Description is the structure's description. A failed load stays failed until the page is reloaded.
The 'Remove' link in the Actions column removes the row at once, with no request and no confirmation.

The Statistics cell starts as the link 'Collect'. Clicking it shows 'Loading...' and sends `POST /rest/structure/2.0/cloudmigration/stats/<id>` with body `{}`, polling through the shared transport while the answer holds only `jobId`. The answer is cached per id for the page, so a removed and re-added row shows it again without a request, or joins a running request. On failure the cell shows 'N/A' and cannot be retried until the page is reloaded.

With `size` 0 the Statistics cell shows 'Empty structure'. Otherwise it shows lines of a bold label and a value, each only when its value is non-zero, in this order: 'Size:' only when `size` differs from issues + folders + memos + pages + generators + effectors; 'Manually added issues:'; 'Projects:' (`projects` joined by ', ', only when issues are present and the list is not empty); 'Folders:'; 'Memos:'; 'Pages:'; 'Generators:'; 'Effectors:'. The generators value is the count followed by the non-zero kinds in brackets. Example: size 12, issues 5, folders 1, generators 2, inserters 1, groupers 1 gives 'Size: 12', 'Manually added issues: 5', 'Folders: 1', 'Generators: 2 (inserters: 1, groupers: 1)', with a non-breaking space after each kind's colon. Kinds are listed as inserters, extenders, groupers, filters, sorters. With no non-zero kind the brackets are empty (as the original does).
